members.name: Great Moravia
members.note: the first Slavic state in these lands, broken by the Magyars

members.name: Cyril and Methodius reach Moravia
members.note: Byzantine missionaries bring a Slavonic liturgy and the first Slavic alphabet

members.name: Přemyslid dynasty
members.note: the founding house, from Bořivoj's baptism to the murder of Wenceslas III

members.name: Golden Bull of Sicily
members.note: Frederick II makes the Bohemian royal title hereditary and self-governing

members.name: House of Luxembourg in Bohemia
members.note: three kings from John the Blind to Sigismund; Bohemia's imperial century

members.name: Charles IV
members.note: king of Bohemia and Holy Roman Emperor who made Prague the empire's capital

members.name: Charles IV crowned emperor
members.note: the Bohemian king takes the imperial crown in Rome

members.name: Lands of the Bohemian Crown
members.note: Charles IV's legal frame binding Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, alive on paper until 1918

members.name: Kutná Hora silver boom
members.note: the mines that minted the Prague groschen and paid for the golden age

members.name: Jan Žižka
members.note: the blind Hussite commander who never lost a battle; birth year approximate

members.name: Hussite Wars
members.note: a religious revolution that beat five crusades, ended at Lipany

members.name: Habsburg rule in the Czech lands
members.note: Ferdinand I's election opens four centuries under Vienna

members.name: Bohemian Revolt
members.note: the Protestant estates' rising that opened the Thirty Years' War

members.name: Battle of White Mountain
members.note: two hours outside Prague that ended Czech independence for three hundred years

members.name: Execution of the 27 Czech lords
members.note: the rebel leaders beheaded on the Old Town Square, still marked by 27 crosses

members.name: Bohemian Counter-Reformation
members.note: forced re-Catholicisation, mass emigration and the Bohemian Baroque that came with it

members.name: Germans in the Czech lands
members.note: seven centuries of German settlement in the borderlands, ended by expulsion

members.name: Czech National Revival
members.note: scholars rebuild a written language and with it a nation

members.name: František Palacký
members.note: wrote the national history and the political programme that followed from it

members.name: Bohemia as Austria's workshop
members.note: the Czech lands carry most of the monarchy's industry, and the wealth to leave it

members.name: Alfons Mucha
members.note: the poster style of Paris, then the Slav Epic back home

members.name: Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk
members.note: the professor who argued Czechoslovakia into existence and then presided over it

members.name: Czechoslovakia
members.note: the joint state of Czechs and Slovaks, from its declaration to the Velvet Divorce

members.name: Munich Agreement
members.note: Britain, France, Germany and Italy hand away the borderlands without a Czech in the room

members.name: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
members.note: six years of German occupation, ended by the Prague uprising and the Red Army

members.name: Expulsion of the Germans from Czechoslovakia
members.note: some three million people moved out under the Beneš decrees, emptying the borderlands

members.name: Communist coup of February 1948
members.note: Gottwald takes full power in a fortnight; the last free election was 1946

members.name: Communist Czechoslovakia
members.note: four decades of one-party rule, from show trials to the Velvet Revolution

members.name: Prague Spring
members.note: 'socialism with a human face', eight months long, ended by Warsaw Pact tanks in August

members.name: Alexander Dubček
members.note: the Slovak party leader of the Prague Spring, returned as speaker in 1989

members.name: Jan Palach's protest
members.note: a student burns himself on Wenceslas Square against the country's resignation

members.name: Normalization
members.note: Husák's twenty grey years of purges, censorship and bought-off quiet

members.name: Charter 77
members.note: a few hundred signatures that gave the dissent a name and a documented voice

members.name: Václav Havel
members.note: playwright, prisoner, then the last Czechoslovak and first Czech president

members.name: Velvet Revolution
members.note: six weeks from a beaten student march to the end of communist rule, without a shot

members.name: Velvet Divorce
members.note: the state dissolves by agreement on New Year's Day; no referendum was held

members.name: Czech Republic
members.note: the Czech half goes on alone

members.name: Czech accession to the European Union
members.note: joins with nine others in the largest single EU enlargement

members.name: Out of Africa dispersal
members.note: the successful spread of modern humans out of Africa across Eurasia

members.name: Polynesian expansion
members.note: the greatest feat of open-ocean seafaring, Tonga and Samoa to Hawaii and New Zealand

members.name: Zhang Qian opens the western routes
members.note: a Han envoy's thirteen-year mission maps the road west

members.name: Silk Road
members.note: the caravan network linking Han China to Rome; usually dated from the Han opening to the Ottoman capture of Constantinople

members.name: Indian Ocean monsoon trade
members.note: seasonal winds carry a sea trade older and richer than the Silk Road

members.name: Trans-Saharan caravan trade
members.note: camel caravans trade salt for gold across the desert

members.name: Marco Polo
members.note: the Venetian whose book of the East Europe half-believed for two centuries

members.name: Ibn Battuta
members.note: travelled some 120,000 km across the Islamic world and beyond; death year contested

members.name: Zheng He
members.note: the Ming admiral of the treasure fleets, born a Muslim in Yunnan; birth year approximate

members.name: Age of Discovery
members.note: European ocean voyaging from Henry's caravels to a mapped world

members.name: Christopher Columbus
members.note: died still insisting he had reached Asia

members.name: Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape
members.note: the southern tip of Africa is passed and the sea road to Asia is open

members.name: Vasco da Gama reaches India
members.note: the first sea route from Europe to India, and the end of the spice middlemen

members.name: First circumnavigation of the globe
members.note: Magellan's expedition comes home under Elcano with 18 of 270 men; he died in the Philippines

members.name: Search for the Northwest Passage
members.note: four centuries of ships trying to sail over North America, ended by Amundsen

members.name: Manila galleon route
members.note: 250 years of Spanish silver crossing the Pacific to buy Chinese silk

members.name: James Cook
members.note: three voyages that turned the Pacific from rumour into chart

members.name: Cook charts eastern Australia
members.note: the east coast is mapped and claimed, opening the way to British settlement

members.name: Lewis and Clark reach the Pacific
members.note: an overland crossing of the new United States, guided in part by Sacagawea

members.name: Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration
members.note: a generation of sledging expeditions, dated from the Belgica to Shackleton's death

members.name: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
members.note: reached on 14 December, five weeks before Scott, who died coming back

members.name: Roald Amundsen
members.note: first through the Northwest Passage and first to the South Pole; lost in an Arctic rescue flight

members.name: First ascent of Everest
members.note: Hillary and Tenzing on the summit, on the ninth British attempt

members.name: Space Race
members.note: eighteen years from the first satellite to the Apollo-Soyuz handshake

members.name: Gagarin orbits the Earth
members.note: 108 minutes that made a human being the first thing of ours to leave the planet

members.name: Voyager 1 enters interstellar space
members.note: the farthest human object crosses the heliopause; confirmed a year later
